Temporal focus:

T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Strait of Hormuz disruption, supply/demand misalignment, U.S. midterm election dynamics, inflation re-ignition
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — structural "security premium" in oil, persistent supply deficit of ~4.3M bpd, depleted buffer capacity

Synopsis:
Brent crude has broken $100/bbl for the first time in six weeks, driven by escalating U.S.-Iran military conflict and Houthi strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure. Roughly 10M bpd (~10% of global demand) remains offline. The U.S. SPR sits at its lowest since 1982. The IEA projects a 4.3M bpd annual supply shortfall. Analysts warn the market has minimal shock-absorption capacity left, and at least one prominent voice (Currie, Abaxx Markets) frames the price surge as structural, not transitory — a growing geopolitical "security premium."

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US stocks, US investments?
Relevance: NO — Primary focus is oil markets and Middle East supply disruption; the U.S. angle (SPR, inflation, midterms) is secondary but present.

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
